title: QA: Wait Clocks, Visual Checks, Page Sending And Pictures
eyebrow: QA · eight steps for you to follow

short.lead: Everything in the approved plan is built and tested here; I need you to try it on your PC in eight short steps and tell me whether it passes.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what I checked.
items: Round 1: the banner ran off the phone screen

A reviewer helper looked at the screenshots with fresh eyes and marked all three written criteria FAIL. It saw the blue banner cut off mid-word at the right edge, and a console error in the capture report.

items.alt: A phone screenshot where a blue banner runs past the right edge and its text is cut off
items.caption: Round 1, before the fix.

items: A builder fixed the causes, not the symptoms. A second, fresh reviewer marked all three criteria PASS, and the check of the written record said the work was done. Nobody asked you anything in between.

items.alt: The same phone screenshot with the banner fitting the screen and its text wrapped on two lines
items.caption: Round 2, after the fix.

items: Pages stay whole when sent alone
A copy of the proposal page sent alone had 5 of 5 pictures broken. Pictures now live inside the page file. An old page with folder pictures went from 2 broken pictures to 0 when repaired in place.

items.alt: Today a picture is left in a folder and breaks; now it is inside the page file
items.caption: One file, pictures included.

items: A wait ends at its deadline
On real processes: a check that succeeds after 2 seconds exits 0; one that never succeeds with a 4-second deadline exits 3 after 4 seconds. By default the first check is at 60 seconds, then every 60.

items.alt: A timeline: first check at one minute, then every minute, ending at done, stalled or deadline
items.caption: The wait clock.

items: `verify.py` passed 1428 of 1428 and `tools/verify_tools.py` exited 0 on the merged code, run by me with nothing else running. Several real faults turned up on the way and were fixed; they are listed under Changes.

items: Follow the numbered steps in Wrap-up. Three of them are commands I could not run on your machine, and each says so.

changes: new
Wait clocks (#560 to #563)
Every wait has a test for when it is finished, a deadline and a check every minute.

A settings file for the numbers, waitfor.py (the script that runs a wait), a guard refusal for background launches with no timeout, a reminder for waits nobody checked, and the rule in "Nothing fails silently". A switch group named waits turns off the parts that block you.
chg
Pictures inside pages (#556, #557)
The builder stores pictures in the page and checks a copy opened alone.
No more pictures folder beside a page. A picture over 1 MB or linked from the web is refused. Two checks look for pictures that would break: a scan of the page, and a copy opened in an empty folder.
new
Page sending (#558, #559)
A made or changed page that was not sent blocks the turn once.

The builder ends with a line saying to send the page, and a page write is followed by a reminder. A hook (an automatic step that runs before each send) opens the page alone and repairs old folder pictures in place, never blocking the send.
new
Visual capture and loop (#564 to #567)
Screenshots, video, frame sheets, a written record and a reviewer each round.

visualcheck.py captures phone and desktop in light and dark, records video and builds a sheet of timestamped frames, measuring how much moved between them. A skill (a saved set of instructions for Claude) runs up to four review rounds. A turn that changes a visual file must now show a real capture, a record check and an image read.
chg
Faults found by running real data
Six faults that only real pages and real transcripts showed.

The picture check missed pictures that appear only when a row is tapped. The repair rebuilt QA pages from git. The reminder about unchecked waits fired wrongly when a prompt merely mentioned a tool. Test runs collided. The injected rules went over their size limit. Long commands were squeezed into a one-character column on a phone. All fixed.
chg
Where the build differs from your approved design
Three places where the build differs; the reasons are in the decisions log.

Old pages are repaired by embedding pictures in place, not rebuilding from source. The wait rule sits inside "Nothing fails silently". The reviewer returns its verdict lines and the main session saves them. See docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md.
chg
Fixed after your QA: the visual reminder is quiet on pages
Zero reminders in two real reruns, down from one and two.

Pages that carry the page builder's mark, or the handover-page meta tag, are no longer treated as visual files. Replaying your two real sessions: 1 firing before, 0 after; 1 before, 0 after. Real reruns on the fixed build: 0 and 0. A plain test page is still checked.

unverified: Not run on your PC: the cloud session could not attach to your computer, so the three commands in Wrap-up are untested on Windows.

Two real sessions on Linux exercised the send reminder, the send hook and the in-place repair. The "block once if a made page was never sent" path only ran on recorded transcripts and made-up payloads, because the test agent always sent its pages.
The visual check's false-alarm rate is unmeasured: only one transcript of 15 turns was available.
Video and frames were proven for the phone in light only; Unity and game capture is only written down.
The injected rules are 6 characters under their size limit, so the next rule added must make room first.
